title: ADT R27A-BK3 EDSFF E1.S and E3.S to PCIe Slot Review
gist: A teardown of the ADT R27A-BK3, an approximately $60 Amazon/AliExpress adapter card that mounts an EDSFF E1.S or E3.S NVMe SSD into a standard PCIe Gen5 x4 slot with an onboard 4-pin PWM blower fan. The single shared EDSFF 1C connector accepting both E1.S and E3.S drives is the technical detail that matters, and the fan's presence signals that thermals, not electricals, are the gating issue when EDSFF drives leave purpose-built server chassis.

insights.claim: The EDSFF 1C connector is electrically shared between E1.S and E3.S drives, so a single PCIe x4-to-EDSFF adapter slot accepts either form factor without a separate SKU.
insights.speaker: Eric Smith
insights.so_what: A common connector lowers the switching cost between E1.S and E3.S for OEMs and buyers, which reduces standards-fragmentation risk for EDSFF adoption and lets backplane and connector suppliers amortize one design across both.
insights.quote: Since it is a shared connector, that means we can install either E1.S or E3.S SSDs into the slot here.
insights.locator: There is also a PCIe x4 to EDSFF 1C SSD

insights.claim: Low-cost EDSFF-to-PCIe adapters are now available for roughly $60 on Amazon and AliExpress, putting datacenter E1.S and E3.S SSDs within reach of workstation and homelab systems that have no EDSFF bays.
insights.speaker: Eric Smith
insights.so_what: A cheap adapter ecosystem creates a secondary-market outlet for used and surplus EDSFF drives, which supports resale values and gradually normalizes EDSFF outside hyperscale — a leading indicator for the form factor displacing U.2/2.5in.
insights.quote: For about $60, you can get an adapter with a fan to fit an EDSFF drive into a PCIe slot.
insights.locator: Recently, we purchased a few of these low-cost E1.S and E3.S PCIe adapters

insights.claim: The same adapter family is also sold in a U.2 variant, indicating vendors are hedging across both the legacy U.2 and newer EDSFF drive interfaces rather than committing to one.
insights.speaker: Eric Smith
insights.so_what: Continued U.2 SKU production shows the installed base is still large enough to serve; watch for U.2 variants disappearing from these catalogs as the practical marker of EDSFF crossover.
insights.quote: There are different versions, including a U.2 version, so make sure you are buying the correct model.
insights.locator: You can find what we purchased on Amazon

insights.claim: The reviewer deliberately bought the fan-equipped version of the EDSFF adapter rather than the bare passive one because of doubts that a PCIe slot environment supplies enough airflow for an EDSFF SSD.
insights.speaker: Eric Smith
insights.so_what: EDSFF drives are designed for front-to-back chassis airflow; moving them into general-purpose systems forces added active cooling, a reminder that EDSFF density gains are paid for in datacenter airflow and fan power budgets.
insights.quote: We purchased the fan versions because we were not confident we could get enough airflow through the bare units.
insights.locator: Recently, we purchased a few of these low-cost E1.S and E3.S PCIe adapters

insights.claim: The ADT R27A-BK3 uses a 4-pin PWM blower fan driven off a standard fan header, and its I/O bracket serves mainly as a mounting point and airflow vent rather than carrying external connectors.
insights.speaker: Eric Smith
insights.so_what: The design confirms cooling, not signal integrity or connectors, dominates the card's physical volume — the practical limit on how many EDSFF drives can be retrofitted into a conventional slot-based server.
insights.quote: The I/O plate is mostly just there to hold the card in place and provide vents for airflow.

insights.claim: The ADT R27A-BK3 terminates in a PCIe Gen5 x4 edge connector, and a separate PCIe Gen4 version of the same adapter is sold alongside it.
insights.speaker: Eric Smith
insights.so_what: Gen5 x4 adapters at commodity prices show Gen5 signal-integrity engineering has reached the low-cost accessory tier, a datapoint on how fast PCIe generations diffuse down the value chain ahead of Gen6.
insights.quote: Here is the bottom edge with the PCIe Gen5 x4 connector. There is a Gen4 version of this, so make sure you are getting the version you need.

insights.claim: The adapter card is physically large because it must simultaneously house an E3.S SSD, a blower fan and a converter board on one PCIe card.
insights.speaker: Eric Smith
insights.so_what: Card area, not slot bandwidth, is the binding constraint for EDSFF retrofits, meaning slot-based systems will never match the per-rack-unit density of native EDSFF backplanes.
insights.quote: The card itself is large because it needs to fit an E3.S SSD, a fan, and then a converter board.
insights.locator: ADT R27A-BK3 EDSFF E1.S and E3.S to PCIe Slot Review section
